ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 1:8 ratio of high-intensity (white/light grey) to low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels across the visible fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary surface consists of low-intensity dark pixels. Distinct high-intensity (white) blobs are concentrated at the distal left tip and inferior central junction (peduncle attachment). Sparse, stochastic high-intensity mottling (2-8 pixel diameter) is distributed across the interior of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an interior pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees; notch depth occupies approximately 16% of the total fluke vertical height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude micro-serrations visible along the distal 30% of the trailing edge on both lobes. The medial sections of the trailing edge adjacent to the notch exhibit a smoother, near-linear pixel boundary.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetric convex curvature extending from the median notch to the lateral tips, with a subtle posterior-directed sweep at the distal margins.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Densely clustered high-contrast white circular nodes at the terminal apex of the left lobe; isolated, lower-intensity circular spots distributed stochastically across the mid-section of the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Three distinct, sub-parallel horizontal light-intensity linear streaks located on the central-right lobe; two faint diagonal linear marks on the lower quadrant of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent, irregular high-contrast calcified mass or scarring at the far left fluke tip, disrupting the dark pigmentation boundary.
other_distinctive_markers: Transverse high-intensity horizontal bands located at the interface between the peduncle and the fluke base.
